en: Solid gallium metal will melt into a liquid pool if you hold it in your bare hand for a few minutes.
Iron nails actually gain mass when they rust because the iron chemically combines with invisible oxygen from the air.
Milk appears to be a uniform liquid, but it is actually an emulsion of tiny liquid fat droplets suspended in water.
Both extremely hard diamonds and soft pencil lead graphite are made of the exact same pure carbon atoms.
Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide that sublimates directly into an invisible gas without ever melting into a liquid first.
A mixture of cornstarch and water acts like a solid when you punch it but flows like a liquid when poured.
Honey is a supersaturated solution that contains significantly more dissolved natural sugars than water can normally hold at room temperature.
Silica aerogel is a solid material made of 99 percent empty air, making it one of the lightest solids known.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar creates a fizzy chemical reaction that produces carbon dioxide, the exact same gas humans exhale.
Mercury is the only common metal on Earth that remains completely liquid at normal room temperature instead of being solid.
Water is highly unusual because it expands and becomes less dense when it freezes into solid ice, causing ice to float.
Brass is not a single element but a solid mixture of copper and zinc atoms blended together at the atomic level.
